A great warship hull lies snapped clean in half, its severed decks exposed to the void, girders and cabling trailing from the wound.
A gutted carrier spills its dead fighters from a cracked-open hangar, the little hulls drifting out in a slow frozen stream.
Frozen explosion-scars blacken the flank of a dead cruiser, its hull pocked with weapon-impacts, every window dark and cold.
A bridge tower sheared clean from its hull drifts slowly apart, navigation arrays still mounted, dead screens facing the eternal dark.
Cold silent weapon-batteries sit locked in their last firing positions, barrels aimed at nothing, the gunners long gone to vacuum.
A reactor-section blown outward leaves a vast cavity in the ship's spine, its edges curled back like scorched black petals.
Loose hull-plates tumble end over end through the debris field, paint still bright on their outer faces, darkness on their inner sides.
Dead running-lights line the hull in long cold rows, their lenses intact, never to flash again in any living harbor.
A breach in the pressure hull vents a slow plume of frozen vapor, crystals catching distant starlight, drifting outward in silence.
Rows of dark portholes stare outward from a listing hull, each one a black eye looking into the void with nothing behind it.
A superstructure reduced to twisted girders stands bare against the stars, its deck-plating stripped away, every interior frame exposed and buckled.
A destroyer's stern hangs free of its forward hull, its drive-bells cold and dark, propellant ice beading on the nozzle lips.
An impact crater punches deep into the port flank, its edges fused smooth by the heat of whatever struck it dead.
A command spine cracked lengthwise lets the ship sag open at its center, bulkheads visible in cross-section like a diagram of ruin.
Drifting escape-pod hatches hang open on torn hinges, the pods themselves long gone or never launched, the dark bays behind them empty.
Sensor masts bent and snapped trail from the hull like broken antennae, their dishes warped, their feeds dead for years or centuries.
A frigate hull rolled onto its beam-ends drifts slowly, its keel facing the stars, its topside lost in its own shadow.
Missile tubes along the ventral hull gape open and empty, their doors blown back, the launchers fired dry in some final desperate salvo.
A crew compartment section peeled open by internal pressure reveals bunks, lockers, and corridor bulkheads to the vacuum, frozen and perfectly still.
Fuel-transfer lines hang severed from a docking collar, their ends sealed by frozen fluid, swaying faintly in gravitational drift.
A point-defense turret sits cocked at a hard angle, its barrels fused together at the muzzle, ammunition cookoff frozen into the mechanism.
The forward hull of a heavy cruiser crumples inward where something massive struck it head-on, frame ribs folded like crushed foil.
Navigation beacons long dead sit mounted at the bow, their housings intact, their amber lights never again to warn another ship away.
A long gash runs the full length of a destroyer's starboard side, a single continuous wound, the edges dark with ancient fire scoring.
Engine nacelles hang at wrong angles from fractured pylons, cold and unlit, their intake vanes stopped mid-rotation and frozen there forever.
